Estimate a mixed graphical model for continuous and binary variables

Source: R/mgm.R
mgm_fit.Rd

mgm_fit() estimates a mixed graphical model: one network for variables of different types, such as continuous symptom ratings and binary indicators. An edge connects two variables that remain associated after conditioning on all other variables, and an absent edge indicates conditional independence (Haslbeck & Waldorp, 2020), so the network shows which variables are directly related when they cannot all be treated as Gaussian or all as binary.

The function regresses each variable on all others with the L1-penalized (lasso) regression suited to its type, linear for continuous and logistic for binary variables, and selects each variable's penalty by the extended Bayesian information criterion (EBIC). Small coefficients are then removed by a threshold (threshold, default "LW"), and the two estimates of each pair are combined by the AND rule (default) or the OR rule into an undirected edge whose weight is their mean. Variable types are detected from the data or given in types. Each regression is checked against its optimality (Karush–Kuhn–Tucker) conditions; certificate() reports the largest violation. A threshold that removes a coefficient changes the network after fitting, so its certificate is then reported as missing; threshold = "none" keeps it. With moderators, the function instead fits a moderated model in which one variable can change the strength of every edge; see condition().

The result is an undirected network of class psychnet (psychnet), or a psychnet_moderated fit with moderators.

For binary data only, use ising_fit(); for continuous data only, ebic_glasso(). Categorical variables with more than two levels need native = FALSE. The model is the one fitted by mgm::mgm().

Usage

mgm_fit(
  data,
  gamma = 0.25,
  types = NULL,
  nlambda = 100L,
  lambda_min_ratio = 0.01,
  threshold = c("LW", "HW", "none"),
  rule = c("AND", "OR"),
  moderators = NULL,
  weights = NULL,
  na_method = c("pairwise", "listwise"),
  native = TRUE,
  labels = NULL
)

Arguments

data

A data frame or matrix with one row per observation. Columns are continuous, binary, or (with native = FALSE) categorical with more than two levels. With native = TRUE every column must be numeric. Columns with fewer than two distinct observed values are dropped. A character column with more than 10 distinct values is refused as an identifier; convert it with factor() if it is a categorical variable.

gamma

EBIC hyperparameter, a single number >= 0; larger values give sparser networks. Default 0.25.

types

Node types, one per column of data: "g" (Gaussian) or "c" (categorical). Default NULL detects them as mgm::mgm() does: factor and character columns are categorical, and so are numeric columns with at most 10 distinct integer values. Such a numeric column with more than two values is named in a warning, because it changes the model for that node; Likert items often meet this rule. A non-factor column declared "c" with more than 10 distinct values is refused.

nlambda

Number of penalty values on each nodewise path, a whole number >= 2. Default 100.

lambda_min_ratio

Smallest penalty as a fraction of the largest, in (0, 1). Default 0.01. With native = FALSE, leaving it unset uses glmnet's own default, as mgm::mgm() does.

threshold

Threshold on the selected coefficients: "LW" (default), "HW" or "none" (see Details), as in mgm::mgm().

rule

"AND" (default) keeps an edge when both nodewise estimates are nonzero; "OR" when either is.

moderators

Optional moderator: one column of data, by name or by position. The moderated model lets this variable change the strength of every pairwise edge and returns a psychnet_moderated fit, read with condition() and as.data.frame(). Needs at least three variables and does not accept weights. Default NULL.

weights

Optional non-negative observation weights, one per row after missing-data handling. Only their relative sizes matter, as in mgm::mgm(). Requires native = TRUE. Default NULL (unweighted).

na_method

"pairwise" (default) fills each missing value with the variable's mean (continuous) or most frequent level (categorical) and keeps every row; "listwise" drops rows with a missing value. The two agree for complete data.

native

TRUE (default) uses the package's own solver, for continuous and binary variables. FALSE fits each regression with the glmnet package (which must be installed), following mgm::mgm(); it also allows categorical variables with more than two levels, but not weights, and its certificate reflects glmnet's convergence tolerance. A network with a multi-level categorical node cannot be passed to net_predict(). One-hot encoding such a variable is not equivalent: it turns one node into several.

labels

Optional node labels: one per node, or one per input column (labels of dropped constant columns are then discarded).

Value

An undirected network of class psychnet (psychnet); with moderators, a psychnet_moderated fit (see condition()). as.data.frame() gives one row per edge (from, to, weight), certificate() the largest optimality violation of the nodewise regressions (missing when the threshold removed a coefficient), and net_predict() the predictability of each node. The object also stores the node types (types), the number of levels per node (levels, 1 for continuous) and the certificate of the regressions before thresholding (fit_kkt).

Details

Continuous variables are standardized before fitting, binary predictors enter as 0/1 indicators, and the coefficient of a binary response is expressed on the two-class multinomial scale of mgm::mgm() (half the logistic coefficient). Edge magnitudes are therefore comparable with those of mgm::mgm(). A binary-binary edge keeps the sign of its logistic coefficient, whereas mgm::mgm() reports such an edge without a sign; compare those edges on their absolute value. Weak edges near the selection or threshold boundary can differ between the two engines.

With \(\beta_i\) the selected coefficients of variable \(i\), \(q\) the number of its predictor columns (\(p - 1\) for \(p\) continuous or binary variables) and \(n\) the sample size, the "LW" threshold removes coefficients smaller in absolute value than \(\|\beta_i\|_2 \sqrt{\log(q) / n}\), and the "HW" threshold those smaller than \(\sqrt{\log(q) / n}\).

Node order is the column order of data, and a categorical variable with several levels remains one node.

Conditions

psychnet_bad_input when data is not a data frame or matrix, types is not one "g"/"c" per column, a character column looks like an identifier, a non-factor column declared "c" has more than 10 values, a categorical variable has more than two levels or a column is not numeric with native = TRUE, moderators does not name one column or names a dropped constant column, a moderated model has fewer than three variables or is given weights, weights is combined with native = FALSE, native = FALSE is requested without the glmnet package, or gamma, nlambda, lambda_min_ratio, weights or labels is invalid; psychnet_type_promotion (warning) when a numeric column with more than two values is detected as categorical; psychnet_no_converge (warning) when a nodewise regression does not reach its optimum; psychnet_degenerate_sample (warning) when a binary variable takes a single value on every row with positive weight. The last two are raised with native = TRUE.

References

Haslbeck, J. M. B., & Waldorp, L. J. (2020). mgm: Estimating time-varying mixed graphical models in high-dimensional data. Journal of Statistical Software, 93(8), 1-46. doi:10.18637/jss.v093.i08

Foygel, R., & Drton, M. (2010). Extended Bayesian information criteria for Gaussian graphical models. Advances in Neural Information Processing Systems, 23, 604-612.

See also

condition() for the moderated model; ising_fit() for binary data; ebic_glasso() for continuous data; certificate() and glm_lasso_kkt() for the optimality check; net_predict(); psychnet() with method = "mgm".

Examples

set.seed(1)
f <- stats::rnorm(400)
g1 <- f + stats::rnorm(400); g2 <- f + stats::rnorm(400)
b1 <- (f + stats::rnorm(400) > 0) * 1L
d <- data.frame(g1 = g1, g2 = g2, b1 = b1, n = stats::rnorm(400))
fit <- mgm_fit(d)
fit
#> <psychnet> mgm network
#>   nodes: 4   edges: 3   (undirected)
#>   optimality (KKT residual): 1.01e-10
as.data.frame(fit)
#>   from to    weight
#> 1   g1 g2 0.3421962
#> 2   g1 b1 0.3288350
#> 3   g2 b1 0.3589604
